items: Article 32 was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution'.
Right to Property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 and made a legal right under Article 300A.
The Preamble has been amended only once till date, by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26th November 1949 and came into full effect on 26th January 1950.
Fundamental Rights guaranteed under Part III are enforceable by courts through writs under Article 32 and Article 226.
Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) contained in Part IV are non-justiciable guidelines for state policy.
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 added Fundamental Duties under Part IV-A on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
